# Task P3-08: LRCLIB lyrics — the client, the tag text and the `.lrc` / `.txt` sidecar

**Phase:** 3 · **Depends on:** P3-05b (the organizer's sidecar options, on the base branch) · **Suggested tier:** cheap worker · **Estimated size:** M

## Goal
When a song is filed into a library (import now, adoption in P3-04 — both go through `LibraryOrganizer`), Wondarr asks LRCLIB for its lyrics. The unsynced text goes into the file's lyrics tag (the tag writer already writes `TagSet.Lyrics`), and a sidecar with the audio file's base name is written beside it: `.lrc` when LRCLIB has synced lyrics, otherwise `.txt` with the plain text (`docs/architecture/LIBRARY_OUTPUT.md` §7.4, `docs/research/research_metadata_plex.md` §5.4 and §5.9). Lyrics are a nicety: **no LRCLIB outcome — a miss, a 429, a timeout, a malformed body — ever fails or delays an import beyond the client's bounded timeout.** A library can turn sidecars off (`LibrarySidecarOptions.Lyrics`, already parsed).

## Deliverables
1. `src/Wondarr.Core/Lyrics/LyricsOptions.cs` — bound to the `Lyrics` configuration section: `bool Enabled = true`, `string BaseUrl = "https://lrclib.net/"` (absolute http/https), `int RequestIntervalMs = 500` (200–5000), `int TimeoutSeconds = 10` (2–60); a validator `LyricsOptionsValidator : IValidateOptions<LyricsOptions>` in the same style as `AcoustIdOptionsValidator` (find it next to `AcoustIdOptions`).
2. `src/Wondarr.Core/Lyrics/LrclibClient.cs` — `ILrclibClient` / `LrclibClient` (typed `HttpClient`):
   - `Task<LyricsLookup> FindAsync(string trackName, string artistName, int durationSeconds, CancellationToken)` → `public sealed record LyricsLookup(LyricsLookupStatus Status, string? PlainLyrics, string? SyncedLyrics, long? LrclibId)` with `public enum LyricsLookupStatus { Found, Instrumental, NotFound, Unavailable }`.
   - First `GET api/get?track_name=…&artist_name=…&duration=…` (each value with `Uri.EscapeDataString`; **no `album_name`** — the ±2 s duration match is the discriminator, and a differing album title makes LRCLIB miss). 200 → the record. 404 → fall back to `GET api/search?track_name=…&artist_name=…` → an array; take the **first** record whose `|duration − durationSeconds| ≤ 2` and that has plain or synced lyrics or is `instrumental`; none → `NotFound`.
   - A record with `instrumental: true` → `Instrumental` (no text). A record with neither `plainLyrics` nor `syncedLyrics` (both null or whitespace) and not instrumental → skip it (in search) / `NotFound` (in get). Synced only → `PlainLyrics` derived from it: strip every leading `[mm:ss.xx]` time tag (there may be several per line) and drop metadata lines like `[ar:…]`, `[ti:…]`, `[length:…]` (a line whose whole content is one `[key:value]` tag with a non-numeric key); keep the line order.
   - 429 or 503, a timeout, any `HttpRequestException`, a 5xx, a JSON error → `Unavailable` (never throws, except `OperationCanceledException` for **the caller's** token). Log at Debug with the status only.
   - Response JSON: `duration` is a float (`248.0`); unknown fields (`hasWordSync`, `lyricsfile`, `name`, …) ignored. Use `System.Text.Json` with web defaults.
3. `src/Wondarr.Core/Lyrics/LyricsServiceCollectionExtensions.cs` — `public static IServiceCollection AddWondarrLyrics(this IServiceCollection services, IConfiguration configuration)`: options + validator (`ValidateOnStart`), a keyed `RequestSpacingGate` (`src/Wondarr.Core/Metadata/Http/RequestSpacingGate.cs`) with `RequestIntervalMs`, the typed client with `BaseAddress`, `Timeout = TimeoutSeconds`, the same identifying `User-Agent` the metadata clients send (read `AddProviderHeaders` / `BuildUserAgent` in `src/Wondarr.Core/Metadata/MetadataServiceCollectionExtensions.cs`; make the helper `internal` if you need it — accessibility only), and a `RequestSpacingHandler`. **No retry pipeline** (a throttled or failing LRCLIB is simply "no lyrics this time"). Call it from `AddWondarrMetadata` right after `services.AddWondarrPlex(configuration);` (if that line is not on your base branch, put it at the end of `AddWondarrMetadata`).
4. `src/Wondarr.Core/Lyrics/LyricsSidecar.cs` — `internal static class LyricsSidecar`:
   - `string? PathFor(string audioPath, LyricsLookup lookup)` → `Path.ChangeExtension(audioPath, ".lrc")` when `SyncedLyrics` is non-empty, `".txt"` when only `PlainLyrics` is, else null.
   - `string ContentFor(LyricsLookup lookup)` → the synced text (for `.lrc`) or the plain text (for `.txt`), line endings normalised to `\n`, ending with exactly one `\n`.
5. `src/Wondarr.Core/Importing/LibraryOrganizer.cs` — wire it in (constructor gains `ILrclibClient lrclib` and `IOptionsMonitor<LyricsOptions> lyricsOptions`, after `coverProcessor`):
   - **Before tagging**, when `lyricsOptions.CurrentValue.Enabled` and `request.Media.DurationMs` is known and > 0: `FindAsync(request.Song.Title, PrimaryArtist(request.Song, request.Credits).Name, (int)Math.Round(DurationMs / 1000.0), ct)`. `Found` → build the tags with `Lyrics = lookup.PlainLyrics` (`TagSet` is a record: `tags with { Lyrics = … }` after `TagSetBuilder.Build`). Anything else → no lyrics tag. The lookup runs **once** per organize.
   - **After a successful placement** (next to `WriteCoverJpg`), when the lookup was `Found`, `LibrarySidecarOptions.Parse(...).Lyrics` is true and `LyricsSidecar.PathFor(finalPath, lookup)` is not null: write the sidecar exactly like `WriteCoverJpg` writes the cover (unique `.partial` name via `DiskOperations.PartialSuffix`, `IDiskOperations.WriteAllBytes` with **UTF-8 without BOM** bytes, `MoveFile`, the partial deleted on every failure, `ApplyCoverPermissions`-style file mode — reuse that method, renaming it to `ApplyFilePermissions`). **Never overwrite** an existing sidecar with that name; also skip when the *other* extension already exists (a user's own `.lrc` wins over our `.txt` and vice versa). Every layout gets sidecars (they are per track, not per folder). A failure is a Warning, never a failed organize.
   - `OrganizeResult` gains `string? LyricsPath = null` (after `CoverJpgPath`), set to the sidecar written.
6. `src/Wondarr.Core/Organizer/LibrarySidecarOptions.cs` — the `Lyrics` property's summary: drop "Read by P3-08." (doc only).
7. `docs/architecture/LIBRARY_OUTPUT.md` §7.4 — one sentence after the sidecar bullet: lyrics come from LRCLIB (`/api/get` with the length, `/api/search` as the fallback, ±2 s), synced → `.lrc`, plain only → `.txt`, an existing sidecar of either kind is never replaced, and no LRCLIB failure fails an import.

## Constraints
- .NET 10, `System.Text.Json`, `Microsoft.Extensions.Http` as already referenced. **No new packages.** Time only via `TimeProvider` (the spacing gate takes it).
- LRCLIB etiquette: the identifying User-Agent on every request, requests spaced by `RequestIntervalMs`, **no retries** and no waiting on `Retry-After` (the answer to a throttle is "no lyrics this time"). No live network calls in tests.
- Sidecars are UTF-8 **without BOM**, `\n` line endings. Never write outside the placed file's folder; never replace a file that exists.
- Never log lyrics text; per-file detail at Debug.

## Acceptance criteria (each must be demonstrated)
1. `dotnet build -warnaserror` → 0 warnings, 0 errors; `dotnet test` → all three test projects pass (paste the summary lines).
2. The tests in 8 exist and pass, including the 404 → search → third-record case against the recorded fixtures and the "existing sidecar is never replaced" case.
3. The existing `ImportServiceTests` and `LibraryOrganizerTests` pass unchanged apart from the constructor helper.

## Out of scope

- Removing a stale sidecar when an upgrade renames the audio file.
